The  staff has a heart for people 🙏
I had to be hospitalized in emergency y'day late evening. I had high fever, constant intense coughing and nausea. My BP had dropped too low as I was unable to eat anything.

My first concern was, of course, financial. And I was relieved as I found that it wasn't so costly, as my Family Doctor, Dr Mohsin Ansari had told me and advised to be admitted there.

Now, In my case, the IV needle was inserted perfectly the first time. However, as I was in a very dizzy state, I sat up putting the pressure on the same hand, causing the vein to blow. And then, when the staff tried to insert another IV neddle, in the other hand, it failed thrice. It pained, no doubt, but it was not due to the staff's negligence,but due to the thinner walls of the veins. This has happened to me at another hospital in the past. I don't endorse lack of skills or expertise.

I am writing this review as a gesture of my gratitude for the service I received and for the benefit of someone who may be looking out for a good clinic.

May God bless you with the healing you need and bless you with good health all through life.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I was admitted to Sapna Hospital for malaria and stayed for 4 days.
It was extremely concerning to see mosquito issues inside the ward while being treated for a mosquito-borne illness. A repellent machine was only provided after repeated complaints.
Hygiene standards were disappointing. I noticed what appeared to be blood stains in saline lines, a dustbin near my bed containing vomit that was not cleared promptly, and an ice pad provided to me that had visible hair on it. Used gloves were also left openly near patient beds instead of being disposed of immediately and bed bugs.
These are basic infection-control practices that should be strictly maintained in any hospital.
Staff behavior at times felt indifferent, and response seemed noticeably quicker when services involved billing.
For a bill of approximately ₹30,000 in just 3 days, I expected a much higher standard of cleanliness, monitoring, and patient care.
I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves hygiene control and patient handling to ensure patient safety.

featured_reviews.name: samita kubal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was recently admitted here for a two-day stay for my stone removal surgery. Initially, I was a bit hesitant after reading some older reviews online. However, a trusted doctor informed me that the hospital management had changed recently and assured me I would have a better experience—and I’m glad to say he was absolutely right.

From the moment I was admitted, I noticed a clear difference in the way staff interacted with patients and their families. The doctors were extremely polite, attentive, and made sure to check every small detail regarding my health. The nursing staff was equally impressive—always smiling, professional, and caring throughout my stay. What truly stood out was how frequently they checked on me after surgery—every 30 minutes, someone was there to ask how I was doing, which made me feel very well cared for.

Another highlight was the hygiene. The hospital floors were spotless, and there was absolutely no unpleasant medicinal smell—something that’s often hard to avoid in hospitals. The housekeeping staff (especially the aunties) were doing an excellent job maintaining cleanliness at all times.

The only reason I’m not giving a perfect experience is the billing process—it took a bit longer than expected. But apart from that, I had a very smooth, satisfying experience and felt that the care I received was truly worth it.

Highly recommended!

Myth: Birth control pills cause infertility. 
This is one of the most common fertility misconceptions — and it stops women from making informed decisions about their reproductive health every single day.

The fact? There is no scientific evidence linking birth control pills to permanent infertility. Oral contraceptives temporarily suppress ovulation while you're on them. Once stopped, your natural cycle gradually resumes. For most women, fertility returns within a few months.

If you've been avoiding contraception out of fear or worrying about past pill use affecting your chances of conceiving  this is your clarity.

That said, if you've been trying to conceive for a while without success, the reason is unlikely to be your contraceptive history. Factors like age, PCOS, blocked fallopian tubes, low AMH, or male infertility are far more common causes worth investigating.

Today I came to Mumbai and it reminded me of this hospital. In 2024 I admitted my sister here but forgot to write the review. So here it is.

It was early morning and my sister had sudden pain in her stomach. Looking at the pain I was quite evident that it was due to stone. As we were near to Parakh hospital we reached there. As per doctor's advice ultrasound was done and as I thought it was due to stone only. We requested doctor to provide some medicine for getting relief from pain so that we can go back to Gwalior and we will take further treatment there as it is our hometown. But he insisted for getting admitted. Considering the pain we decided for getting admitted. They kept giving my sister injections and medicines for holding the pain. Also ran some other tests. After 24 hours they started insisting for surgery. We finally decided to get discharged from the hospital. The total expense that we had to pay for this 1 day was 30000/-
Worse part was that immediately after the discharge the pain returned and my sister was still in the same situation as 1 day before.
At last I went to a medical store nearby and told him about the pain. The medical store guy gave just 1 pill and with that medicine the entire pain vanished and my sister reached back Gwalior via train without any pain.
In Gwalior she took homeopathy medicine treatment and in six months all the stones are gone without any surgery.

So I'm not sure about how this hospital is at present but in October 2024 they literally looted us in just a single day. So beware.
